Article says Spanish until 1797, mostly French settlers; entry says French planters after 1783 and British capture 1797; article has no 1783 date, left out. Left out zoology and economy details.

Article says 220-280 AD with majority view; entry says third century; consistent. Article's 'Cao Wei founded by Cao Cao' in literature section vs Cao Pi proclaimed emperor: avoided. Left out demographics, politics, sports and recent finds. Article calls 1337 earthquakes; I used only listed years (363, 1033, 1202, 1837 appear in the list).

Entry says Whitehead presented to Austrian commission on 21 December 1866; article gives only 1866; not repeated. Lusitania dated only May 1915 in the article. Article says by 1870 improved up to 900 metres at 6 knots (as stated, though 6.5 knots in 1866 is slightly higher; kept as article).

Article's lead says 'Georg August University' and George II 'on the orders of'; consistent with entry. Article says Gauss taught 'in the 18th century' (his time is partly 19th); wrote only 'began the tradition'. Article dates Hilbert's remark 1934: omitted. Left out rankings, organisation figures, and current people.

Entry says it became capital after Artaxata; article gives only 120-330 CE capital; left out. Article says Vagharshapat 'fifth largest' in lead and '4th largest' in geography; used fifth (lead). Left out mayor, sport, twinning. Persian rule dates as article.

Article says Egypt continued as UAR 'until formally dissolved by Anwar Sadat in September 1971' and 'name changed 2 September 1971'; consistent. Left out Lebanese crisis, Iraqi coup, Yemen, Six-Day War and the Ben-Hur remark. Article says Nasser 'initially resisted total union' per Boghdadi; hedged as 'is reported'.

Entry says the Roman inscription is 'the northernmost Roman monument in Central Europe'; article says it was long the northernmost known evidence until the fort at Mušov and camps near Olomouc and Hulín were found: left the 'northernmost' point out of the text. Left out 2026 Capital of Culture, sport and population tables.

Article calls the Entente 'informal' and based on the 1894 alliance, 1904 Entente cordiale and 1907 Anglo-Russian Entente; entry consistent. The Anglo-Japanese/Franco-Japanese material shortened. Article says the Entente 'is not an alliance'; entry 'informal alignment' consistent.

Article says 'Mauryan founded the City of Ujjain' and 'Paramaras built the city': left out as odd. Article names the river both Shipra and Kshipra. Left out smart-city, government, transport and rankings. Entry says Maurya 'urban centres of craft and commerce'; article says 'commercial centre' consistent.

Entry mentions the forced conversion of Iran to Twelver Shi'ism and the Seljuk and Zand states; article mentions none of this beyond the Safavids and Seljuk-era Nizamiyya; not repeated. Article says madrasa 'likely originated in Khurasan' hedged. Left out title list and modern challenges.

Entry says Nobunaga's successor and unification; consistent. Article lists no 'land survey' as a named event beyond 'surveys of land and production'.
Article says al-Walid resolved in 706 to build; entry says 705-715 built: dates left out except the nine years. Left out 2011 events and Assad regime material.

Entry says devotional cults of the late 1st millennium BCE; article says 7th-4th century BCE for the Bhagavata cults: dates for that development left out. Left out demographic figures and the contested dating of Nimbarka.
